claim: The published optimized D18:PY-IT:eC9 champion J-V result cannot satisfy this repository's stabilized-Pmax useful-work gate because the primary source reports a scanned J-V measurement, not a stabilized maximum-power-point trace.

source.title: Suppressing electron-phonon coupling and energy loss in organic solar cells by modulating donor-acceptor penetrated-interface
facts_used: Figure 5f is described as the J-V curve of the optimal D18-PYIT-eC9 1-0.2-1 device.
The Methods describe J-V acquisition with a Keysight B2901A under AM1.5G and about 5 ms delay time per voltage step.
The main text reports about 20 meV higher Voc, over 18% efficiency, and no sacrifice in Jsc and FF.

important_boundaries: This does not claim the published device lacks real efficiency improvement.
This does not infer stabilized Pmax from scanned PCE.
This does not establish lot-level reproducibility.
The reported approximately 5 ms step delay is a measurement-setting fact, not a stability time constant.
Absence of a stabilized MPP trace in the inspected primary main text is not proof that no such measurement exists anywhere; supplementary or author-held data could change this classification.
falsifier: Provide primary-source or author-released stabilized MPP time-series data for the paired D18:eC9 and D18:PY-IT:eC9 devices with sufficient provenance to evaluate the repository gate.
runtime: Python standard library; tested target versions 3.12, 3.13, 3.14
